newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 24.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Monday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright asks Japan for further efforts to resolve issue of leasing land for U.S. bases in Okinawa in meeting with Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ideda.
-- Chichibu Onoda Cement Corp plans to begin disposing of five types of ozone-damaging chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) at its cement plant in Chichibu, Saitama prefecture, from April 1.
-- Non-life insurers agree to abolish two more premium cartels -- the Japanese Hull Insurers' Union and the Union of Machinery Insurers of Japan.

-- Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said talks to free 72 hostages held in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru are still in their preliminary phase. He said he could not predict how many more weeks the discussions would take.
-- Government to cut by 30 percent local government spending for entertaining bureaucrats in 1997/98 budget.
-- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright urges Japan to join the United States and South Korea in giving food aid to North Korea.
